absent: Numeric values and bit widths of mount and propagation and dentry flags.
Calling contexts allowed to invoke detachment and unmount and propagation helpers.
Lifetime and reclamation rules for mountpoint records and cover records and namespaces beyond pinning shown.
Definition and update protocol of the global event counter and poll wait queue.
Hash table sizes and initialization and resizing for mountpoint and mount tables.
Behavior of the custom dentry comparison path and of placeholder filesystems for covered dentries.
Full memory ordering and grace period requirements for hash and list traversal.
Error handling beyond warnings for duplicate unmount marking and namespace detachment.

findings.text: Mount detachment is offered as a small inline gate that inspects the mountpoint flag on a dentry and does nothing for ordinary dentries, delegating flagged dentries to the full detachment routine.

Detachment from a dentry executes under exclusive namespace protection combined with writer protection for mounts, while dentry unhashing serializes only around the dentry own spinlock. Relevant guards are namespace_excl and mount_writer with dentry spin member d_lock.

Detachment guarantees that after completion no live mount remains stacked on the given dentry, the dentry name is no longer visible for lookup, a global namespace event generation has advanced, leftover cover state has been released, and any temporary mountpoint pin has been dropped; absence of a mountpoint record leaves the dentry otherwise untouched.

Mountpoint records are sharded across a hash table indexed by a mixed function of the dentry address, with collision chains searched by dentry identity; a successful search pins the record by linking a caller owned node into its member list, and unpinning removes that link and allows reclamation. Relevant members are m_dentry and m_hash and m_list and m_covers with caller pin using node and mp and stacking via mnt_mp_list.

Unmounting a mount tree guarantees single marking of every member of the connected subtree, removal of namespace membership for attached members, detachment from parent child visibility, privatization of propagation links, release of namespace references with event refresh, clearing of namespace association, transfer to a global unmounted queue, and conditional notification; optional propagation input widens the doomed set before privatization.

The mount hierarchy is navigated depth first through child and sibling links rooted at the requested mount, terminating at the root, with parent identity test distinguishing a true root where parent points to itself. Relevant members are mnt_parent and mnt_mounts and mnt_child.

Namespace membership is represented by a tree node whose emptiness signals detachment; removal updates cached edge pointers for first and last members, erases the node, clears it, and drops auxiliary visibility linkage when present. Relevant members are mnt_node and mnt_ns and mnt_first_node and mnt_last_node and mnt_ns_visible.

Mount notification coalescing ensures a mount appears at most once on the pending list per hold interval, queuing only when current or previous namespaces carry watches and otherwise adopting the current namespace as previous; one build variant is an empty operation.
Namespace event refresh is idempotent within a generation, updating the stored generation and waking poll waiters only on a generation change, with null input safely ignored.

Detaching a single mount from its parent restores self parenthood and self root as mountpoint, clears any overmount alias that referenced it, and drops child and hash and mountpoint memberships before allowing mountpoint reclamation.

Cover records preserve the mountpoint and covered dentry of an unmounted child, remaining reachable both from the mountpoint cover set and from the surviving parent cover set until the covered dentry itself is torn down. Relevant members are mnt_cover and mnt_mountpoint and mnt_mp with cover linkage via pin and node and m_covers and mnt_covers.

Cover preservation is suppressed for synchronous teardown and requires the parent already be doomed, applying then to children that either requested cover handling or carry a locked propagation attribute.

Privatization of a doomed mount set converges on surviving propagation masters through peer and master traversal with temporary marking, then rewrites master links toward those survivors, migrates slave membership, and clears sharing and marking state while releasing abandoned group identifiers.

Propagation topology traversal favors slave descent for established mounts and otherwise climbs through master and peer and slave relations back toward the origin peer, with group identity defining peers and new unattached mounts recognized by absent namespace association.
Preparation for propagated unmount clears the locked attribute on counterparts of the target mountpoint found across the propagation neighborhood of the parent, and assumes a non root starting mount.

Mount lookup by parent plus dentry is hash based under read side protection, returning the matching child when present; for doomed parents it may instead return a placeholder filesystem distinguished by directory versus non directory character of the dentry when a corresponding cover exists, otherwise reporting absence.

Mount hash sharding combines scaled addresses of the parent vfsmount and the dentry with shift and mask selection over a global table. Relevant globals are mount_hashtable with m_hash_shift and m_hash_mask.
Directory character for mount and lookup decisions encompasses both ordinary directory entries and automatic directory entries as determined by entry type.

Propagated unmount selection proceeds from broad candidate gathering to iterative elimination of revealing or shifting members, then resolution of locked chains, re anchoring of surviving overmounts onto live ancestors, and finally merging of accepted victims into the doomed set.

Candidate handling marks visited mounts to avoid reprocessing, skips entire propagation subtrees already covered, tolerates a single surviving overmount child while treating other survivors as blocking, propagates blocking marks upward, and cuts locked chains at the highest unlocked ancestor, with singly doomed members detached from namespace and parent visibility.

Surviving overmounts of accepted victims are re anchored to the nearest live ancestor while preserving their mountpoint record, with mountpoint replacement updating parent and dentry and hash and list memberships, maintaining a special alias when a mount covers its parent root, and requesting notification.

Attachment of a mount to a parent establishes parent and mountpoint record and covered dentry links, registers hash visibility keyed by parent plus dentry, appends to parent child membership, and records root covering as an overmount alias. Relevant members are mnt_parent and mnt_mp and mnt_mountpoint and mnt_hash and mnt_child and overmount.

Read side dentry lookup walks a hash bucket without blocking, validating parent identity and combined hash length and byte equality and hashed state and sequence stability, returning the candidate plus its sequence for caller validation; concurrent rename may yield false negatives unless the caller holds outer rename stabilization, and dentries with custom comparison use a separate path. Relevant members are d_parent and d_name and d_seq and d_hash.

Lock free name comparison relies on atomic name pointer sampling and guaranteed string termination and later sequence retry to tolerate torn length or concurrent moves, with explicit unhashed rejection to close a lookup versus unhash race.

Name equality is provided in two build variants, one comparing word sized units with masked tail handling and one comparing byte by byte, both reporting mismatch versus full equality over the requested length.

Observed mount and teardown indicators include MNT_UMOUNT and MNT_LOCKED and MNT_SYNC_UMOUNT for persistent flags and T_SHARED and T_MARKED and T_UMOUNT_CANDIDATE for transient propagation state and UMOUNT_COVER and UMOUNT_PROPAGATE and UMOUNT_SYNC for teardown modes, with newness defined by absent namespace association.

Observed dentry indicators include DCACHE_MOUNTED denoting mountpoint status and DCACHE_OP_COMPARE selecting custom comparison, with DCACHE_DIRECTORY_TYPE and DCACHE_AUTODIR_TYPE distinguishing ordinary and automatic directory character.
Detachment of mounts covering a dentry and dropping of dentry visibility are exposed for use beyond this file set.
Bulk privatization and propagation unlock and propagated unmount expansion and release of propagation group identifiers are exposed as cross file operations.
Lookup of a child mount by parent and dentry together with changing and establishing mountpoints are exposed as cross file operations.
Lock free lookup of a child dentry by parent and name with sequence output is exposed as a cross file operation.
